series: Cleaning $22 vs $55 Short follow-up 1 of 3 (recurring discount angle)
hook: Every 2 weeks at $245? Only $18.61 is profit
hook_say: Here is how much of a $245 every-2-weeks clean is profit once the 10% recurring discount comes off.

rows.label: Home
rows.why: The kit's example home: 1,800 square feet, 3 bedrooms, 2 full and 1 half bath, 1 pet, an inside fridge and 8 interior windows.

rows.label: Cleaners, round-trip miles
rows.why: You plus one paid helper, 16 miles round trip. Your hours cost your break-even rate, the helper's hours cost the helper rate.

rows.label: One-time price, rounded up
rows.why: Timed by square feet and by room count, the larger one wins, priced at your numbers and rounded up to the next $5: $270 for a one-time standard clean.

rows.label: Every 2 weeks, 10% off
rows.why: Take 10% off for an every-2-weeks client and the visit price is $245.

rows.label: Price floor, zero profit
rows.why: Labor, the helper, vehicle cost at 76 cents a mile and supplies: $226.39 just to cover your pay goal, costs and taxes.

rows.label: Profit per visit beyond your floor
rows.why: That leaves $18.61 of profit per visit. The kit's check line flags it: above your floor, but under your target margin at this frequency. Change the discount or the minutes and watch the line.

note: Example numbers from the kit. Yours go in the yellow cells.
sources: Product #14 Cleaning-Business-Pricing-and-Planner.xlsx from Drive folder 14 zip (Oct 4 build), recalculated in LibreOffice Oct 6, 2026: 4 Quote Builder B7 to B20 and B25, B27 (inputs), B53 270, B54 10%, B55 245, B50 226.39, B59 18.61, B61 check text; 2 Your Numbers B32 76 cents.
